en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Naked (Naggavagga) 26. The Training Rule on Group Robes.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the family supporting the bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to her:
"Noble lady, we shall give robe-cloth to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā—
“You have many duties and much to do,” he said, thereby creating an obstacle.
At that time, the house of that family was burning down.
They complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā create an obstacle to our gift?
In both respects we shall be excluded—deprived of both wealth and merit.
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and lamenting.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires … [as above] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā create an obstacle to the acquisition of robes for the Saṅgha? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā created an obstacle to the acquisition of robes for the Saṅgha?”

“It is true, Blessed One. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her: “… How can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā create an obstacle to the acquisition of robe-cloth for a group? This is not suitable, bhikkhunīs. [The Buddha then gave a discourse on the dangers of creating obstacles. Having rebuked her and given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhunīs: “Bhikkhunīs, a rule of training should be laid down thus: ‘If a bhikkhunī creates an obstacle to the acquisition of robe-cloth for a group, she commits an offense of expiation. [The Buddha then laid down the training rule. “Now, bhikkhunīs, how is there an offense of expiation? If a bhikkhunī, knowing that a group has acquired robe-cloth, creates an obstacle to its distribution by saying, ‘Do not distribute it; let us wait until such-and-such a person comes,’ and she does so out of desire, ill will, delusion, or fear—this is an offense of expiation. [The Buddha then explained the details of the rule. “In this way, bhikkhunīs, this training rule is laid down. “Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule:
‘If any nun should create an obstacle to the acquisition of robe-cloth for a group, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "a bhikkhunī" means... [as before].
... [as before] ... in this context, "bhikkhunī" is intended in this sense.
A "group" (gaṇa) is said to be the community of bhikkhunīs (bhikkhunī-saṅgha).
"Robe" means any one of the six kinds of robes that is suitable for assignment and is of the lowest grade.
"Should cause an obstacle" means:
If she creates an obstacle [thinking], "How might they not give this robe?", there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she creates an obstacle for another requisite, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).

If she creates an obstacle for the robe or another requisite belonging to several bhikkhunīs, or to a single bhikkhunī, or to one who is not fully ordained (anupasampannā), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if she prevents her by pointing out the benefits,
or if she is insane.
"By one who is a first offender.
The sixth training rule is concluded.
